items.q: How should your workspace change across the day?
items.a: **Phase 1 (0–8 h after waking):** bright overhead + forward light, screen at/above eye level, upright posture, narrow visual field for analytic work. **Phase 2 (9–16 h):** dimmer, warmer light; shift toward creative/abstract work. **Phase 3 (17–24 h):** minimal bright light to protect melatonin.

items.q: What is the Phase 1 light rule?
items.a: Max safe **overhead + forward light**; an **open window beats closed glass** for blue wavelengths. By ~**4–5 PM**, reduce overhead and shift toward yellow/red.

items.q: Why does screen height change focus?
items.a: Looking **below nose level** inhibits locus coeruleus alertness. Put the screen at **nose level or above** (stack books if needed); lying down is anti-focus.
Aim **~50/50 sit-stand** — standing > seated > reclined for alertness; feet above waist activates calming circuits. Kelly Starrett: you weren't designed to sit *or* stand all day.

items.q: How wide should your visual work target be?
items.a: Keep the target within **"horse blinders" width (~head width)** — too-wide monitors dilate gaze and break attention. A hoodie/hat can lower effective ceiling for analytic mode.

items.q: What is the 45/5 visual break protocol?
items.a: Every **45 min** of vergence/narrow focus → **5+ min panoramic gaze** (horizon walk). **Do not check your phone** on the break — that is still vergence. Fits inside **90-min ultradian** blocks.

items.q: How long before deep focus kicks in?
items.a: Expect ~**6 min** neurochemical ramp-up (studies show ~**3 min** before task-switch without training). Lighting, posture, and screen height shorten that latency.

items.q: How does ceiling height change cognition?
items.a: The **cathedral effect**: **10 ft vs 8 ft** ceilings measurably shift **abstract vs detail-oriented** cognition. Use high ceilings/outdoors for Phase 2 creative work; low ceilings for Phase 1 analytics.

items.q: Which sounds help or hurt focus?
items.a: Constant **HVAC hum** increases fatigue. **40 Hz binaural beats** (±5 Hz) for ~**30 min** before/during work can improve reaction time, verbal recall, and math via striatal dopamine — pure beats beat rain overlays (**7 Hz + rain impaired** recall).
You pay the distraction **plus** re-engagement time. Face the computer **toward a wall**; don't body-pivot to the door; phone in drawer/safe — interruptions are **deadly to focus**.
